restrictions: Ordinary collision of SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps from the standard IV: two 128-byte messages with the same random first block M0 and second blocks M1, M1' = M1 + DL (differences in words 8..12), then the common padding block. The second block is the transplanted advice pair with A[6], A[7] released over a list generated at import by rule on the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe: 9,701,592 entries in 728 classes, 3,462,264 (a2, W10) keys; the walk constants c9, C9 are shifted by 0x05cefde0. The W17 condition is solved per F9 claw by a generic bit-sliced pass over the 62,400 distinct 18-bit prefixes; a passing prefix is completed, tested on scalar words and, at a key hit, expanded to the classes of its group.

Our accepted ab09e983 (94.0681) with three changes: (a) 2e846bf2's H6 withdrawn: the program stops every window at W_max = 573,465,000 counted operations (guards, 2 ops each, reservations bounded by count) and asserts it (the 2^42 last-window term kept only as margin); a capped window credits only its completed claws, retained fraction r_LB = 0.9930279 (one-sided 99%, 1,080 predeclared windows; premise H1-screen (iv)), conservative stop-selection margin 0.0001 in the divisor (1 - 0.0615907); ceil(B / r_LB) executed windows charged W_max each; (b) exact k4q early exit from position 22 (claws, F9 claws, keys unchanged); (c) F9 factor over 1,080 predeclared windows 802060-803139: 901.6269, trials 10774.5 per distinct claw. Kept: entries as trials, entries tail 2^-74.4783 (H2-entries), mate term (H-W3-uniform), a26bcf74's program, screen, H1-screen, C_W 57,003.18, k4d cap 944. Time 94.0073 (W_max+6 per window, ceiled at 4 decimals). Memory 2^20.0000. Advice 160 bytes. Success 0.39.

heuristics.statement: MODEL (declared, new in this entry). Under the screened chaining-value and window law of the shipped program (a3eb4a8a screen S <= 5, KCAP = 679, DTRY = 8,192, KTRY = 32; windows of 2^26 walk evaluations): (i) distinct claws per window have mean 57,003.18, the unit C_W of B and the cap (60-window panel mean, s.d. 210.99); (ii) [this entry: trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10774.5 per distinct claw, measured on the first 125 F9 claws of each of the predeclared 1,140 windows 802000..803139 (PREDECLARE_NJ68_1115.txt) by a rebuilt count calibrated to the 16-window control 802000-802015 (proof Section 7); the transfer from the first 125 F9 claws of each window to all its F9 claws is declared by this clause; the two full-window checks (802000, 802001) are support, not proof]; (iii) kept chaining values are independent across windows; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws, and a claw's trial-key count is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11 do not depend on the chaining value); the W17 claw constants (w, c) are uniform and independent of (a0, u), as H5 uses; at most 944 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (program cap, k4d line 1101; the cap binds in some windows, and the trial count takes min(D_i, 944)). 9,044.1 (a26bcf74's keys figure, not used by this entry; its trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10774.5 = 681,192.49 x 901.6269 / 57,003.18 rounded down, 681,192.49 = 681,709.27 - 2.5801527 x 200.29, the calibrated entries per F9 claw of the 1,140 windows, proof Section 7) is the joint one-sided 99% lower bound (union bound, 99.5% per factor) (576,745.3 - 2.946713 x 970.3) x (907.1667 - 2.661759 x 25.6780 / sqrt(60)) / 57,003.18 = 9044.17, rounded down: keys per F9 claw on 2,000 F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened windows (16 batches, t(15); one-way ANOVA over 16 windows: F = 0.564 on 15 and 1,984 df), distinct F9 claws per window on the 60 screened 2^26 windows (54,430 in total, t(59)), C_W as the declared model mean; the screen conditions the chaining value on S <= 5, and this premise carries the unscreened keys-per-F9-claw count to the screened law. (iv) Work cap (this entry; 2e846bf2's H6-cap-completion is withdrawn): Under the screened window law of the shipped program with the cap: (iv-a) windows are i.i.d., so over the B / r_LB windows of the search the keys of the claws a capped window completes are at least the fraction r_LB = 0.9930279 of all keys (one-sided 99% ratio-of-sums bound, 1,080 predeclared windows); (iv-b) the F8-passing entries of the completed claws are the same fraction of all entries (a claw's trial count is a function of its own (a0, a1), H1-screen (iii)); (iv-c) H1-screen, H5 and H2-entries hold for completed claws as for all claws. A capped window succeeds at least on the union over the key hits of its completed claws; the stop selection on the claw in progress is covered by (iii); the 0.0001 in the divisor is an extra conservative margin. (v) The cap-completed F9 claw count s_w of a window is independent of its keys' tail-event probabilities P_w (tails: rows 18-39 of each key's pair; s_w: the walk to row 17 and the cap), so E[(s_w - 1) P_w] / E[P_w] <= 898.120, the claw-weighted 99% bound of sum s_w(s_w - 1) / sum s_w over the cap-completed claws of 91463de0's 1,080 predeclared cap-panel windows (point 896.439; full windows of Appendix D: 905.530; cap m_max - 1 = 943). (vi) The p'_k-weighted means over completed-claw key occurrences (p'_k = union probability of key k's F8-passing mates) of E[min(N_k, 3)] and P(N_k >= 4) are at most their complete-list means at uniform w (a key's equal-G structure is set by the key list, not by its mates' rows 18-39 or by its claw's completion). Priced: pi_bar = 1.09e-3, covering both measured values (list mean 1.0718e-3; 1.0825e-3 at 2,000 real F9 claws), and left-out 0.000281038 (99%; no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 independent w).
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and the --attack path of experiments/r39joint_k4.py (screen on) with the shipped advice pair and the list generated at import.
heuristics.extrapolation: Paired participant-run probe, same seeds on both builds, 16 pairs at 2^24 walk evaluations (N = F8-passing entries, K = distinct keys, over the four diagnostic groups, per distinct claw C): unscreened N/C 106.91, K/C 98.56; screened N/C 111.16, K/C 102.24; paired N/C change +0.0552 bit (s.e. 0.0459). Distinct F9 claws per window 907.17 in the 60 screened 2^26 windows against 898.62 in the 48 unscreened windows. The probe supports a nonnegative transfer; it is not a 2^26 panel of the key count: the transfer of the keys-per-F9-claw count is the declared premise. This entry's entries count: one-way ANOVA of the 2,000 claws' entry counts over their 16 panel windows F = 1.362 on 15 and 1,984 df; Taking the first claws of a window is not a selection on the count: on all F9 claws of windows 802000 and 802001 the first 125 average 677,197.7 and 676,356.3 entries against 681,901.6 and 683,853.0 for the rest (Welch z = -0.69, -1.17). Capped-window yield (clause iv): From 1,080 predeclared windows 980000-981079 (2^26 walk evaluations; W_max, seeds and estimator recorded before any run; every window reported): r = 0.993636, s.e. 0.000262, cap fired in 1,080, lowest window 0.9613. Per window the capped yield is exact for the run (stamp method; checked against a capped run on window 803140: 849 claws and 486,760,973 keys, equal; and by the organizer in r39k4-window-small trial 1: 10 claws, the 6 with stamp <= W kept exactly).
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run: 2,000 unscreened claws for the key count, 16 paired 2^24 windows for the transfer, 60 screened 2^26 windows for C_W and the F9 claws per window. This entry: the first 125 F9 claws of each of the predeclared 1,140 windows 802000..803139 (PREDECLARE_NJ68_1115.txt) for the entries count (participant-run; calibrated to the 16-window control); their transfer to all F9 claws is the declared clause (ii). Clause (iv): Participant-run windows on public seeds; the ratio bound is normal-theory (delta method) at n = 1,080; the organizer run checks the cap's stop on a small window, not the 2^26 yield.

heuristics.statement: The W17 pass costs at most 143,633 (exact early exit; fewer on most blocks) operations per evaluated F9 claw: 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks), a formula of the table evaluated and asserted by the program, with no folded or claw-specialised code. A survivor costs 711 + 563 per class tested, at most 5,215; a key hit at most 49,472 (the at most 8 classes of its group as mates); the screen 4 + 183 per first-block draw plus 3 per discarded draw; the one-time setup, the rule generator included, is charged 1,107,473,556 operations. Each work-cap guard costs 2 operations, inside W_max. The program executes ceil(B / R_LB) windows, R_LB = 0.9930279, asserted at import, and the program bounds A.m.o by W_max and charges W_max+6 per executed window, including the six main-loop operations, so the ceil margin of K x C_W (K = 10,061) is not charged.
heuristics.scope: The counted pass, survivor, key-hit and screen paths and setup and the work-cap guards of experiments/r39joint_k4.py.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact counts of the program; the organizer run asserts the pass cost per claw, planted survivor costs and, on one screened window, the screen charge of every draw (187 kept, 190 discarded).
heuristics.limitations: The 2^30 part of the setup is an allowance for the import's other statements.

heuristics.statement: MODEL premise of this entry (screened scope). For an F8-passing listed entry of class 01 drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, entry) triples of the attack, windows drawn under the screened law and weighted by their trial count, in a claw passing F9 with W17 equal to the advice value, the two 39-step compressions collide along the advice differences with probability at least 2^-74.4783: the lower of the 14-run organizer pooled mean (2^-74.4594) and class-01 mean (2^-74.4783, the replica's 4 x c01 estimator) of r39-mate-01..14, rounded down, by a rule written before the class counts existed. A mean of organizer-executed runs, not a lower confidence bound. a26bcf74's H2-transfer (2^-74.3238, keys and designated mate) is cited only as the keys value. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1).
heuristics.scope: Rows 18 to 38 of the advice trail after rows 0 to 17 hold, for class-01 trial entries of windows of the screened law.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 14 organizer runs (one uniform listed entry per batch, (a0, a1) by the claw model) to class-01 entries of screened windows over the whole attack. Arm J (participant-run, real unscreened claws, an entry per lane) gives 2^-74.3828.
heuristics.limitations: A mean, not a bound: the one-sided 99.9% lower bound of the pooled runs is 2^-74.6588. The class-01 mean rests on 466 class-01 hits.

heuristics.statement: A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 are fixed to the advice values; (A[6], A[7]) range over the listed entries of the fibre 0x3cc9eebe; for every listed entry both messages follow the advice state-difference trail through step 15, W9 is C9 + 0x05cefde0 - a1 and W16 is one value per claw. Constructing and selecting the advice pair costs at most 2^43 compressions (2^42.545 by the accounting of proof Section 9), added to the claimed time; the offline fibre search costs at most about 2^31.1 compressions (estimated from the tools' loop counts), inside the remaining 2^41.1.
heuristics.scope: The one-time construction of the 160-byte advice pair of 5f8e6192; the list is generated at import by the rule of proof Section 2.5.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exhaustive enumeration over all 2^32 a3 with the real two-message trail checked on every entry at four points (0 failures); the rule reproduces that list exactly; the organizer run checks one entry of every group at the advice point.
heuristics.limitations: The 93-pair campaign was run by the pair's authors and is charged at its declared cost.

heuristics.statement: Screened-window scope: for the windows of the screened law, windows are independent (fresh first blocks, each drawn and screened independently). Trials are distinct (a2, kappa) keys with at least one listed entry passing F8 in a claw passing F9: trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10774.5 per distinct claw (H1-screen (ii), proof Section 7: the calibrated F8-passing entries per F9 claw on the 1,140 windows 802000..803139 times the F9 factor of the 1,080 windows 802060-803139). Each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw (a uniform claw constant); events in different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)] (the priced quantity is E_w[min(N_k(w), 3)] <= pi_k). Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1-screen. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and family-wise over all keys (alpha = 0.001) E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 1.36e-2. Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 1.341e-3 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise over all keys at alpha = 0.001). The priced co-hit and left-out terms are the p'_k-weighted means over the keys of completed claws of E[min(N_k, 3)] and P(N_k >= 4), bounded by the complete-list means under H1-screen (vi); the per-key family-wise bounds (1.36e-2, 1.341e-3) hold for every key and are kept for reference. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the designated-mate tail events, as for the hit events themselves. Real 2^-32 hits: 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over the 48 windows; 3 compressed F8-passing mates against 6.85 expected (P = 0.09, disclosed). The program tests every key hit; success is priced by second-order Bonferroni over all hits on designated-mate events (proof Section 7), divisor 1 - 0.0615907 (stop-selection margin 0.0001 included) with the cross-claw term on the claw-weighted claw count (H1-screen (v)) and the within-claw term on the key-mean co-hit rate (H1-screen (vi)); no premise between the tails of different hits is used.
heuristics.scope: The amplification over the B / r_LB windows of the screened, capped program.
heuristics.extrapolation: Keys with an entry in F8 per F9 claw 576,745.3 (s.e. 970.3, 16 batches of 125 claws); per-claw s.d. 57,687; F9 claws per window from the 60 screened windows (mean 907.1667, s.d. 25.6780).
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run counts (2,000 claws, 60 screened windows). The organizer's dispersion test is a scaled spot test on four fixed groups; independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and windows is the premise, not a measurement.

heuristics.statement: Premise H-W3-uniform: given a hit (an F8-passing entry whose pair collides along the advice differences), the entry's message word W3 is uniform over 2^32. By the exhaustive enumeration of rows 18-19 (proof Section 7, Appendix D), mate j with offset d_j can follow the advice through row 19 only if W3 lies in B_{d_j} = {W3 : Delta(W3, d_j) in D = P - P, Delta != 0}, empty for 14 of the 20 offsets and of at most 120,832 elements for the others. Hence E[X_i | T_i] = sum_j P(S_j | T_i) <= 7 x 120,832 / 2^32 = eps = 1.9693e-04 (a key has at most 7 other mates), sum over keys of P(U_k) >= (1 - eps/2) sum over entries of P(T_i), and eps/2 = 0.000099 is in the divisor. No independence between mates is assumed.
heuristics.scope: Every key hit: the program compresses every F8-passing mate (k4q); the enumeration covers every W3 and every mate offset of the list.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer test of the premise (the r39-mate manifest prediction): r39-mate-01..14 pin the W3 of all 1,888 hits (867 carrier clusters) by their organizer-recorded digest48 (proof Appendix E); 0 lie in the union of the B_d (expected 0.24; falsified at 3 or more); per-bit chi-square 24.7 on 32 df (falsified at 62.49); 638 F8-passing mates traced, none past row 19. Price without the premise (disclosed, not priced): the strict hit-weighted 99% cluster bound 0.01716 gives eps 0.12015, divisor 1 - 0.137206, time 94.1835. Not used: per-cluster 4.605 / 867 and per-hit 4.605 / 1,888.
heuristics.limitations: H-W3-uniform is a premise about one distribution (W3 given a hit); 1,888 hits test it only coarsely at the 2.8e-5 scale, and the B_d are structured sets (near 2^18 elements each). The r39-mate hits come from the replica's start-state law with the claw model for (a0, a1), one listed entry per batch, not from the attack's screened claws; the test is carried to screened claws as the entries tail is (H2-entries).

heuristics.statement: Given the claws, the W17 events of distinct keys are dispersed as independent trials. Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event of probability 2^-7 on every key of four groups (every 50th) with an entry in F8, in every F9 claw of the four organizer windows: 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws; acceptance region fixed in the manifest and asserted.
heuristics.scope: Four of the 200 groups, all F9 claws of the four organizer windows of r39k4-window-small.
heuristics.extrapolation: The attack's event has probability 2^-32 on the same keys and words.
heuristics.limitations: Four groups only, for run time; the groups are fixed by the program.

heuristics.statement: MODEL (declared, new in this entry; answers the reviewer-added implicit premise H-public-seed-unbiased by name). The participant-run public-seed panels that set this entry's score - the 1,140-window entries panel (seeds 802000..803139, first 125 F9 claws per window, proof Section 7), the 1,080-window cap-yield panel (seeds 980000-981079, r_LB = 0.9930279, proof Section 7 and Appendix F), the 1,080-window F9 panel (seeds 802060-803139, 901.6269, Appendix D) and the historical score-setting panels (Appendix B's 60 screened windows, C_W = 57,003.18; Appendix A's 48 unscreened windows, seeds 1000-1047) - are representative of the production window law of the shipped program, and the statistics reported from them are not materially biased by the choice of seeds, estimator, revision point or multiple comparisons. What is recorded rather than declared is printed in proof Appendix G: both predeclaration texts verbatim with their MST timestamps (PREDECLARE_NJ67_1115.txt 2026-11-15 16:48, PREDECLARE_NJ68_1115.txt 2026-11-15 18:06), the dated sequence of every declaration (S160 2026-11-12 23:26, S161 2026-11-13 14:33, S162 2026-11-13 17:56, W_max 2026-11-14 13:05, the cap panel 2026-11-14 21:26), the contiguous public seed ranges, the tool identity (f8count2.py sha256 34f65c7075a144f3256749413dcb1ebb1a5d649fef87ba5c9658c95112b65155 (rebuilt count of F8-passing listed entries per F9 claw, first 125 F9 claws per window, k4 off); r39joint_k4.py sha256 458910183f9f814d... = accepted 1bb2ccf3; the cap program c72e5d36...380e3a), the all-window accounting (every one of the 1,140 seeds present with its 125 counts matching its stored mean, the 42 twice-counted seeds agreeing on raw counts and counted once, seven empty duplicate/placeholder files leaving no seed missing, every cap-yield window reported with a skipped window counted as zero in both sums, the lowest single-window ratio 0.9613 printed), the one declared estimator (batch (window) means, one-sided Student-t at 0.995 per factor union-bounded to a joint 99%, the form of the accepted H1-screen (ii), restated in both predeclarations before the runs) and the calibration c = 0.9989414 fixed on the 16 control windows before the 1,124 new counts ran. Stated exactly, as in Appendix G: that record supports reproducibility and complete reporting of the declared ranges, not unbiasedness; the timeline is partial, because PREDECLARE_NJ68_1115.txt precedes the entry-count runs it governs but reuses the seeds already run for the F9 factor, whose F9 and work outcomes were therefore known when it was written, so it is not a commitment made before all outcomes on those seeds were known; and the organizer-executed manifest experiments run small windows, not these panels at their size. Organizer execution of this submission's r39k4-window-small (experiments/manifest.json, fields hypothesis and scope: 4 unscreened windows of 2^21 walk evaluations, k4 and check mode on) reproduces the participant's small-window claw, F9 and sampled distinct-key diagnostics: distinct claws per window (233, 222, 256, 232), F9 claws per window (7, 11, 4, 1) and per F9 claw D = distinct keys with an entry in F8, K = those in the declared 2^-7 W17 event, sums per trial (sum D, sum K, Pearson, claws) = (59,256, 437, 6.5188, 7), (67,492, 518, 7.9839, 10), (17,882, 142, 0.7772, 4), (1,872, 7, 4.0067, 1), over 4 of the 200 groups (proof Section 11 lines 204 and 209; Appendix G line 480). These are participant counters reproduced in organizer execution: the organizer's experiment report records them as untrusted_participant_observations and leaves internal predicates, work and extrapolation unverified; D is a distinct-key count, not the calibrated entry count in T. Transferring these supporting observations to screened, full-size, all-group entry yields and cap/dependence statistics remains explicitly heuristic and is this heuristic; limits in proof Appendix G, lines 478-480.
heuristics.scope: Every score-setting statistic taken from the participant-run public-seed panels: the entries factor and its calibration (1,140 windows), the F9 factor (1,080 windows), the cap retention r_LB and the cross-claw claw-weighted term (1,080 windows each), C_W (60 windows), the keys-per-F9-claw count carried from the 48 unscreened windows, and the seed, estimator, revision and multiple-comparison choices behind all of them.
heuristics.extrapolation: The transfer of the supporting small-window diagnostics of r39k4-window-small (participant counters reproduced in organizer execution, recorded in the organizer's experiment report as untrusted_participant_observations; manifest.json fields hypothesis and scope; proof Section 11 lines 204 and 209, Appendix G line 480) - distinct claws per window, F9 claws per window and distinct keys per F9 claw on 4 unscreened windows of 2^21 walk evaluations over 4 of the 200 groups - to the screened, full-size, all-group entry yields (calibrated entry counts, not distinct keys) and the cap-retention and co-hit/dependence statistics at search scale, including the unscreened-to-screened law change; the entry-to-key and selection transfer stays in the declared premises that carry it (H1-screen (ii)); and the transfer of the declared contiguous public-seed ranges, all windows reported, to the production window law of the shipped program. No organizer holdout nonce or organizer-selected seed set measures these quantities at full panel size.
heuristics.limitations: The panels are participant-run. The entries predeclaration reuses seeds whose F9 and work outcomes were already known, so its timeline is partial. The hash, duplicate-seed and count-to-mean checks support reproducibility and complete reporting, not unbiasedness. One rule and one estimator were declared and applied to every window, but that the declared rule is itself unbiased for the production law is the premise, not a measurement. The first-125-claws transfer inside a window is the separate premise H1-screen (ii). r39k4-window-small gives participant counters reproduced in organizer execution (untrusted_participant_observations; internal predicates, work and extrapolation unverified by the organizer) on four unscreened windows of 2^21 walk evaluations, with distinct-key (not entry) counts over 4 of the 200 groups and no screened yield tuples; the organizer runs do not execute the large panels, and there is no holdout nonce. A frozen-program, organizer-selected holdout measuring the entries, F9 and cap-yield quantities on organizer-chosen seeds would be stronger evidence than this record.
